page: Microsoft Azure D48ls_v7 is a Dlsv7-family virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes a 480 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). This instance is configured with 96.0 GB of system memory, yielding a low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or GPUs, though it is premium storage capable.

In benchmark evaluations, the D48ls_v7 demonstrates strong performance in compute-heavy and instruction-dependent tasks. The Passmark CPU score of 66,066.16 and the extended instructions score of 59,793.2 place it in the top 25% tier, reflecting the efficiency of its Intel Xeon architecture. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches a top-tier 15.17 GB/sec, while multi-threaded decompression registers at 303.78 GB/sec. For database and memory-bound operations, the instance achieves 79.02 million operations per second in Redis SET tests and a Passmark database score of 22,291.38. However, the 96.0 GB memory capacity represents a clear tradeoff, limiting its utility for memory-intensive datasets despite its high compute density.

The qualitative cost profile of the D48ls_v7 is defined by its high compute density relative to its memory footprint. By minimizing memory overhead, the instance offers a resource-efficient configuration for CPU-bound workloads that do not require large RAM allocations. It is suited for web serving, with a static web serving throughput of 75.36 GB/sec, as well as CPU-based machine learning inference, where it processes 7B model prompts at 243.16 tokens per second. Other appropriate workloads include data compression, cryptography, and compute-heavy batch processing.
